newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Sept 30, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - The rush by notebook manufacturers to bundle Microsoft Corp's Windows NT on new offerings could backfire for corporate buyers, as proprietary extensions designed to address NT's missing mobile features may result in incompatible products, PC Week reported in its Sept. 30 issue.

International Business Machines Corp's Software Group outlined how its strategy to shift toward Sun Microsystems Inc's Java language and networking computing will mean major changes in current and new products.

INFOWORLD - Cambridge, Mass.-based Open Group successfully convinced software vendors at a Microsoft Corp.-sponsored ActiveXstakeholders meeting to designate it the guardian of the ActiveX component integration technology, InfoWorld reported in its Sept 30 issue.

Open Group will apparently now begin to manage future collaborative development and enhancements, licensing, and specifications of the ActiveX object technology. But Microsoft has retained significant influence of the technology's near-term future by choosing influential members of a key planning committee, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - Netscape Communications Corp Chief Executive James Barksdale is looking beyond the browser wars with Microsoft to the battle for the corporate Web market, Information Week reported in its Sept. 30 issue.
Microsoft plans to merge Rational Software Corp's Rational Rose object modeling technology with its forthcoming Visual Basic 5 in time for a planned January release, Information Week reported.

COMMUNICATIONS WEEK - Leading Unix and router vendors are moving swiftly to fortify their systems against a security hole that has left Internet service providers vulnerable to network crippling attacks, called synchronized number sequence attacks.

Netscape Communications Corp is readying software to help information systems managers better administer intranets with their existing management tools, Communications Weeks reports in its Sept. 30 issue.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Microsoft Corp will begin beta testing its Normany Internet server software this week, which promises to open up new opportunities for computer resellers to expand their external Web sites, CRN reported on Sept. 30.

COMPUTERWORLD - Microsoft Corp is retooling its VisualBasic application development software for the Internet in an attempt to keep users from switching to Sun Micro's Java language, Computerworld reported in its Sept. 30 issue.

Silicon Graphics Inc is preparing a series of servers and workstations in a major product revamp, but a recently discovered flaw in one of the chips that power the systems could mar the rollout, Computerworld reports.
COMPUTER RETAIL WEEK - Novell Inc, 3Com Corp, Bay Networks and other local area network companies are getting very serious about their retail connections, Computer Retail Week reported Sept. 30.
Entertainment software publishers are concerned about the spate of losses or decreased earnings among entertainment retailers, CRW reported in its Sept. 30 issue.
MACWEEK - Claris Corp unveiled version 2.0 of its HTML authoring software, Claris Home Page only two months after launching the first version, MacWeek reported Sept. 30.

The new version will support built-in Web site publishing, QuickTime and Shockwave plug-ins and other features, and it will be available for public beta in mid-October. It is expected to ship in December at a retail price of $99.00. Upgrades from version 1.0 are free, MacWeek reported in its Sept. 30 issue.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - European chip makers last week reversed themselves and agreed to eliminate European Union tariffs on chips, removing a key barrier to a global Information Technology Agreement, EBN reported in its Sept. 30 issue.

There are many signs in Japan that U.S. semiconductor distributors are gaining more than the previous toehold of the Japanese electronics market, as electronics buyers are becoming more sensitive to the high prices they are paying and want more foreign made chips, EBN reported Sept. 30.

ELECTRONIC ENGINEERING TIMES - As Intel Corp prepares to formally unveil its first processors that use its MMX multimedia technology, a group of software developers is talking about a purported performance limitation, EE Times reported in its Sept. 30 issue.

As the U.S. electronics industry debates the grand divide between the PC and the TV, Japan's consumer giants like Sony Corp, Matsushita and Toshiba Corp will unveil solutions for both environments at the Japan Electronics Show this week, EE Times reported.
